articles.title: China tightens export controls on tunnel-boring machines from 18 November — International Relations / Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A clean case of "weaponised interdependence": India's metro, rail and highway tunnelling depends on imported TBMs, and China is adding them to its dual-use export-licence regime just as India–China ties are being normalised post-Galwan. Good for Mains answers on supply-chain resilience, Atmanirbhar manufacturing and India–China relations.
**Key facts:**
- China's Commerce Ministry (MOFCOM) announced the change, reported by Reuters; it takes effect **18 November 2026**. Exporters will need a licence under China's export-control law and dual-use rules. The same update reportedly adjusted controls on drone-related items and dredgers.
- The Hindu's digest adds that heavy machinery used above **3,000 m** (e.g., plateau-type shotcrete machines) is covered, with licences for sensitive or disputed destinations and prior registration for others; this detail rests on one source.
- Precedent: in **Sept 2025** Germany's ambassador said Chinese customs had held at least **three Herrenknecht TBMs** bound for Indian projects; they were later released, and Herrenknecht decided to **produce in India**.

**Notebook:** GS2 – International Relations (India–China); GS3 – Economy (infrastructure, manufacturing).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS / Mrunal "India and its neighbourhood" – India–China; Mrunal economy pillar "Infrastructure". Add a cross-link: rare-earth and fertiliser curbs (2025) → TBM curbs (2026) as a pattern of China's export-control leverage.

articles.title: Aditya-L1's VELC produces Doppler velocity images of the solar corona — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The coronagraph's spectroscopy yields plasma-velocity maps that show whether a coronal mass ejection (CME) is moving toward Earth. This ties space-weather forecasting to satellite and power-grid safety, and is a fair Prelims candidate (payloads, orbit, L1).
**Key facts:**
- Scientists at the **Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA), Bengaluru** generated Doppler images from the **Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC)**, the largest of Aditya-L1's seven payloads. Positive velocity = plasma moving away from the observer; negative = toward.
- Aditya-L1: launched **2 Sept 2023** on **PSLV-C57**; halo orbit around Sun–Earth **L1** (~**1.5 million km** from Earth) since **6 Jan 2024**; design life 5 years.
- Payloads: **4 remote-sensing** (VELC, SUIT, SoLEXS, HEL1OS) and **3 in-situ** (ASPEX, PAPA, magnetometers).

**Notebook:** GS3 – Science & Technology (Space).
**Static anchor:** Spectrum "Science & Technology – Space" / Mrunal Sci-Tech pillar: ISRO missions. Add a table: Aditya-L1 payload → what it measures; cross-link to solar flares, CMEs and space weather in the Geography (Sun's layers) notes.

articles.title: Reuters coins "heat storm" for supersized, long-lasting global heat events — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A new framing for climate-extreme data that links to Mains GS1/GS3 questions on heat waves, El Niño (already in the 15 Oct briefing) and disaster preparedness. The concept is journalistic, not an official IPCC/WMO category, so avoid over-claiming in answers.
**Key facts:**
- A heat wave = at least five consecutive days of abnormally high temperature; a **heat storm** covers at least **1% of the globe** at its peak (about half the size of Canada).
- **"Vera"**: largest on record, **367 days** (2023–24), nearly **85%** of the globe. **"Raimundo"**: current event since **28 Feb 2026**, touching almost **three-quarters** of the planet.
- Heat storms averaged about **5 a year** in the 1960s and about **102 a year** this decade; a cascade begun on **6 July 2008** has not stopped.
- **IMD criteria (static)**: heat wave in plains when max temp ≥ **40°C** (37°C coastal, 30°C hills) with departure ≥ **4.5°C**, or an absolute ≥ **45°C**.

**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (climate change); GS1 Geography (climatology).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS "Climate Change – impacts"; NCERT Class XI *Fundamentals of Physical Geography*. Add the IMD heat-wave criteria box and link to NDMA heat-action plans.

articles.title: PM Internship Scheme after the March revamp: wider pool, higher stipend, attrition still the test — Economy (Schemes)
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A scheme-evaluation staple: demand-side participation and drop-out rather than funding. Useful for GS3 (employment, skilling) and GS2 (scheme design).
**Key facts:**
- Launched as a pilot in **Oct 2024** with a goal of **1 crore** internship opportunities over five years; nodal ministry: **Ministry of Corporate Affairs**.
- March 2026 revamp (ThePrint): stipend **₹5,000 → ₹9,000**, age **21–24 → 18–25**, duration **12 months → 6–9 months**, employer pool **500 → ~2,000** firms; MSMEs, statutory bodies and GCCs now participate.
- Round 3 (from April; offers till December, joining till January 2027) has 30,000+ joiners against a 1.1 lakh target. Sources differ on past drop-out figures (ThePrint ~54% in Round 1, ~34% in Round 2; another digest reports completion of ~43% and ~39%), so treat exact attrition numbers as provisional.

**Notebook:** GS3 – Economy (employment and skilling).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal "Employment & Skilling" pillar; Economic Survey chapter on employment. Add a one-line row: PMIS vs PMKVY vs Apprentices Act, 1961, with the "completion rate" metric.

articles.title: Department of Financial Services (Ministry of Finance): Financial Inclusion Saturation Campaign, 21 Oct – 31 Dec 2026 (statement 19 Oct)
articles.text:
- **What:** A nationwide last-mile drive covering about **2.70 lakh Gram Panchayats and Urban Local Bodies** to saturate financial-inclusion schemes.
- **Activities:** bank camps to enrol people in **PMJJBY, PMSBY and Atal Pension Yojana**; open **PMJDY** accounts; re-KYC; C-KYC IDs; nomination updates for accounts and lockers; Kisan Credit Card applications (to saturate PM-Kisan beneficiaries) and PMFBY enrolment ahead of Rabi; awareness on digital frauds and unclaimed assets under **"Aapki Poonji, Aapka Adhikar"**.
- **Why it matters:** moves from account-opening to *insurance, pension and credit* coverage; links with SLBC machinery. Monitored by state administrations, banks and the Department of Finance.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Economy (financial inclusion); GS2 Governance (delivery).

articles.title: Ministry of Power / CEA: Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) — PIB backgrounder on India's storage push (19 Oct)
articles.text:
- **What:** PSPs pump water to an upper reservoir when power is cheap/surplus and release it at peak demand; long-duration storage (typically 6–20 hours) that supports frequency regulation, black-start capability and absorbs renewable curtailment. Types: open-loop (natural water bodies, e.g. Tehri) vs closed-loop (isolated reservoirs, e.g. Kundah).
- **Key figures:** per the Ministry of Power (Rajya Sabha reply, July 2026) **11 PSPs (15,870 MW) are under construction** and 6 more (8,140 MW) are CEA-concurred; commissioning phased 2026–2032. The backgrounder (reported via secondary summaries) puts operational capacity at ~7.43 GW and identified potential at ~345 GW across 320 sites *(these two figures single-sourced; verify on PIB)*.
- **Enablers:** 2023 PSP development guidelines; MoEFCC B2-category appraisal; CEA DPR timeline cut from 90 to 50 days; inter-state clearance dispensed with; **100% ISTS charge waiver for 25 years** (contracts awarded by 30 June 2028); tariff-based competitive bidding guidelines (2025).
- **Notebook:** GS3 Economy/Infrastructure (energy, renewable integration).

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry: India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement enters into force, 20 Oct 2026 *(UPDATE — negotiations/signing covered earlier; new is entry into force)*
articles.text:
- Signed 27 April 2026. Indian exports get duty-free access to New Zealand from day one; sensitive Indian items (dairy, sugar, edible oils, certain meat/agri goods) are excluded from India's concessions; apples, kiwifruit and Manuka honey get limited access via tariff-rate quotas/seasonal windows.
- NZ commits to facilitate **USD 20 billion** investment into India; mobility: 5,000 temporary employment entry visas, 1,000 working-holiday visas a year, and post-study work rights (up to 3 years STEM; up to 4 years doctoral).
- **Notebook:** GS2 IR; GS3 Economy (trade).

articles.title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in India (17–22 Oct); talks with EAM Jaishankar in Mumbai today — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The visit is the first high-level US engagement while the India–US trade deal is unfinished and the Russian-oil question is open. It is a good case for Mains questions on "strategic autonomy vs. economic pressure" and on how India handles tariff and sanctions leverage. The MEA calls the visit a chance to advance cooperation across the pillars of the "Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership".
**Key facts:**
- Rubio is in India 17–22 Oct. He holds talks with EAM S. Jaishankar in **Mumbai on 20 Oct**, then goes to **Jamnagar (Gujarat)** for energy talks.
- Agenda: energy, trade, investment, defence, critical and emerging technologies.
- Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal says the **first phase of the trade deal is finalised and in legal drafting**; it will be operationalised only when India gets a "competitive advantage". An **interim framework** was announced by the White House in February.
- US Ambassador Sergio Gor says President Trump is expected to decide **within about 10 days** whether to invoke sanctions powers that could hit buyers of Russian oil and gas. India says its energy choices follow national interest and market conditions.
- The MEA rejected claims that Rubio "bypassed Delhi", noting that hosting dignitaries outside the capital has been routine for about a decade.

**Notebook:** GS2 – International Relations (India–USA).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS / Mrunal "India and its neighbourhood & major powers" – India–USA. Add a one-line timeline: interim framework (Feb 2026) → phase-1 legal drafting (Oct 2026) → sanctions decision (~end Oct). Cross-link to energy security (Russian crude).

articles.title: CWC reservoir bulletin: storage at ~68.6% of live capacity across 178 major reservoirs; the South is the weak spot — Geography
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** An El Niño year plus a deficient monsoon is stressing water storage. Useful for GS1 (monsoon, water resources), GS3 (irrigation, food security) and GS2 (inter-state water disputes, e.g., Cauvery, Krishna).
**Key facts:**
- The CWC bulletin of **15 Oct 2026** (as reported by a UPSC digest; the full bulletin was not accessed) puts storage at **126.717 BCM, or 68.58%** of the usable (live) capacity of **178 reservoirs**.
- Earlier, a 24 Sept CWC update showed about **70% storage against a 10-year average of 76.62%**. **South India was at about 50%**; cumulative monsoon rainfall was about 12% below normal, and parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka were declared drought-hit.
- Reported weak spots: Aliyar, Idukki, Somasila and Mettur reservoirs; Pennar, Cauvery and Krishna basins show the largest deficits. Narmada and Mahanadi basins are above normal.
- **CWC:** under the Ministry of Jal Shakti; formed 1945 (renamed 1951); HQ New Delhi; monitors reservoir storage, issues flood forecasts, handles dam design and safety.

**Notebook:** GS1 Geography (Indian monsoon, water resources) / GS3 Agriculture (irrigation).
**Static anchor:** NCERT Class XI *India: Physical Environment* – Climate; Spectrum "Water Resources". Add today's figure to a "storage vs 10-year average" tracker and cross-link to the 15 Oct WMO El Niño note.

articles.title: Draft lab-animal rules, 2026: 3Rs, registration and Institutional Animal Ethics Committees — Environment (Animal Welfare)
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A draft rule-making story that links the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 with Article 51A(g) (compassion for living creatures). Animal-rights groups such as PETA India have asked for withdrawal, arguing it weakens oversight. Good for "Statements" MCQs on regulators and committees.
**Key facts:**
- Issued by the **Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying** on **6 Oct 2026** as **G.S.R. 864(E)**; comments invited until **6 Nov 2026**.
- Built on the **3Rs: Replacement, Reduction, Refinement**.
- Breeders, traders and establishments register with the **CCSEA** (generally valid 3 years); experiments need prior approval of the CCSEA or the **Institutional Animal Ethics Committee (IAEC)**, which has **nine members** including a scientist, a veterinarian, an external member and a socially aware member.
- Use of protected wildlife, wild/stray animals and **non-human primates is restricted**, subject to scientific justification and permission.
- Which earlier rules it supersedes was not stated in the source I read; check the notification text before writing it into notes.

**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (animal welfare) / GS2 Governance (delegated legislation).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS – Environment: "Animal welfare laws"; Laxmikanth – Fundamental Duties (Art. 51A(g)). Nudge: add a table of Animal Welfare Board of India vs. the experiments committee, with legal basis for each.

articles.title: National Strategic Trade Command Centre (NSTCC) launched by Piyush Goyal — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A data-governance reform for foreign trade: one dashboard for policymakers across DGFT functions. Prelims angle is what it covers; Mains angle is "data-driven policy and ease of doing trade".
**Key facts:**
- Launched in New Delhi on **15–16 Oct 2026** (reports differ on the exact day) by the **Commerce & Industry Minister**.
- Gives a **consolidated view** of trade performance, export-promotion schemes, regulatory approvals, application processing and operational indicators.
- Covers DGFT areas such as **Importer-Exporter Code (IEC), Advance Authorisation, EPCG, Certificate of Origin, SCOMET**, and restricted imports/exports.
- The minister asked for **regular Inter-Ministerial Committee meetings** to clear pending applications.

**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (external sector, trade facilitation).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal – "Foreign Trade Policy and DGFT"; Ramesh Singh – Chapter on Foreign Trade. Nudge: add a one-line glossary of IEC, EPCG, Advance Authorisation, SCOMET.

articles.title: TDB–DST backs QNu Labs with ₹150 crore from the RDI Fund for quantum-secure and sensing technologies — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Distinct from the 16 Oct DRDO QKD field trial: this is about funding and the wider "quantum-secure and sensing" stack, including navigation without GPS. Pairs with the National Quantum Mission in notes.
**Key facts:**
- **₹150 crore** from the **Technology Development Board (TDB, under DST)** through the **Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund**, as **optionally convertible debt**; total project cost **₹300 crore**. Recipient: **QNu Labs, Bengaluru**.
- Four pillars: identity security (quantum-secure PUFs, quantum-safe TPMs), location integrity (**quantum magnetometers**, navigation without GPS), network security (chip- and satellite-based **QKD**), time integrity (indigenous high-precision **atomic clocks**).
- Goal: take technologies from **TRL 4–5 to TRL 9** under "Quantum Secure and Sensing Networks".

**Notebook:** GS3 Science & Technology (quantum, indigenisation).
**Static anchor:** Spectrum / Shankar IAS – "Quantum technologies". Nudge: add a TRL ladder note and a cross-link to the 16 Oct DRDO QKD entry.

articles.title: UPSC (constitutional body): Commission completes 100 years (1 Oct 1926 – 1 Oct 2026) — *PIB backgrounder, via PIB-summary sites, 19 Oct*
articles.text:
- **What / why it matters:** The Public Service Commission began on 1 Oct 1926 as an advisory body (Chairman and Members appointed in London). The Government of India Act, 1935 made consultation mandatory. On 26 Jan 1950 the Federal PSC became UPSC, an independent constitutional body under **Part XIV, Arts. 315–323**. Directly relevant to the merit-based civil service and the "steel frame" theme.
- **Key facts:** ICS exam introduced in London 1855; first held in India (Allahabad) 1922; Lee Commission (1924) recommended a statutory PSC; Kothari Committee (1979) gave the three-stage exam; Mains restructured to four GS papers in 2013; Universal Registration Number introduced May 2025; AI-based facial authentication used for CS (Prelims) on 24 May 2026 (about 5.5 lakh candidates). Women's share among recommended candidates rose from 6% (1952) to 31.2% (CSE 2025). Current Chairman: Dr Ajay Kumar (since 15 May 2025).
- **Notebook:** GS2 Governance / Polity (constitutional bodies).

articles.title: Parliament (Rajya Sabha Secretariat / Lok Sabha): India at the 153rd Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) Assembly, Arusha, Tanzania (early–mid Oct 2026; PIB release 19 Oct)
articles.text:
- **What / why it matters:** India's delegation was led by **Harivansh, Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha** (members incl. Anurag Singh Thakur, Sasmit Patra, Lata Wankhede). Assembly agenda: an emergency item on climate-related disasters (proposed by Nepal; covers the Himalayan region), a general debate on good governance and inclusivity, and panels on UN conflict-prevention machinery and AI and the future of work. Outcomes reported: **Arusha Communiqué** and resolutions on persons with disabilities and climate resilience in the Himalayas. **Milton Dick** (Speaker, Australian House of Representatives) elected the **32nd IPU President** (9 Oct).
- **Notebook:** GS2 Polity / International Relations (parliamentary diplomacy; IPU is the global organisation of national parliaments, HQ Geneva).

articles.title: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare (ICAR-CPRI): Kufri Jamunia — India's first biofortified purple-fleshed potato (highlighted in PIB-linked summaries, Oct 2026; variety released 2024)
articles.text:
- **What / why it matters:** Addresses "hidden hunger" through biofortification; rich in anthocyanins, Vitamin C, carotenoids, iron and zinc. Yield 32–35 t/ha; recommended for the North Indian plains. *(Light item — variety is not new, PIB feature is a highlight.)*
- **Notebook:** GS3 Agriculture / Science & Tech.

## Also worth a line (headline-level, not verified from PIB text)
- KAUMARACON-2026 (3rd International Conference on Kaumarabhritya, All India Institute of Ayurveda) inaugurated by the Vice-President; AYUSH Start-up Portal, AyuDIVA, Vamana App and Panchakarma Assessment App launched.
- PIB feature on rail/road connectivity in J&K (USBRL, Chenab Bridge, Zojila Tunnel breakthrough June 2026) — largely overlaps PM GatiShakti coverage of 12 Oct, so skipped.

## Scheme-in-focus: Green Highways Policy, 2015 (MoRTH/NHAI)
- **Ministry:** Road Transport & Highways (implemented by NHAI).
- **Objective:** Create green corridors along National Highways to reduce pollution and erosion and generate local employment.
- **Key features:** (1) Plantation, transplantation, beautification and maintenance of roadsides; (2) execution through SHGs, State Forest Departments, private agencies; (3) Plantation Cell monitoring via NHAI regional offices; (4) 2026 norms: 80% ROW coverage, 90% survival; NH-GCI monitoring with ISRO-NRSC.
- **Coverage:** National Highway network (about 1.47 lakh km).
- **Significance:** Links infrastructure growth with climate mitigation and carbon sinks.

articles.title: India rejects OIC resolutions on J&K; says Pakistan "misused" the grouping — International Relations
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** The OIC Council of Foreign Ministers (Baghdad, 17–18 Oct) adopted resolutions with anti-India references. MEA (19 Oct) rejected them as "malicious, biased and false" and said the OIC has "no locus standi whatsoever" on India's internal matters. It urged members to "reform this organisation". A good case study of India's Gulf/West Asia outreach versus the Pakistan-led OIC agenda, and of India's stand on sovereignty.
- **Memorize:** OIC founded 1969 (Rabat), HQ Jeddah, 57 members; India is neither member nor observer. MEA line: J&K and Ladakh are "integral and inalienable parts of India".
- **Notebook:** GS2 International Relations
- **Static anchor:** Mrunal/Shankar IAS "India and West Asia / Multilateral groupings" → add OIC with a timeline (1969 founding → 2019 Abu Dhabi guest-of-honour invitation → recurring J&K resolutions). *Nudge: cross-link to the Article 370 and J&K notes.*

articles.title: Zero sugar diversion for ethanol in 2026-27: OMC tender bars sugar-based feedstock and cuts the maize price — Economy / Agriculture
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Oil marketing companies (tender by BPCL, issued 16 Oct) seek about 11 billion litres for the supply year from November for E20. Ethanol from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses is excluded; the government set sugar diversion to zero for 2026-27 because of weak rain in key States and high retail sugar prices. Food-versus-fuel trade-off is a classic Mains theme.
- **Memorize:** Allowed feedstocks: maize, broken rice, FCI surplus rice, damaged foodgrains, C-heavy molasses. Maize ethanol price cut to ₹68.86/litre from ₹71.86. India has reached E20; E25/E27 and flex-fuel options are being explored.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Economy / Agriculture
- **Static anchor:** Mrunal "Energy security and biofuels" and Ramesh Singh "Agriculture" → update National Policy on Biofuels 2018 notes. *Nudge: add a "food vs fuel" box with the 2026-27 sugar example.*

articles.title: India and carbon-market coalitions: the Open Coalition on Compliance Carbon Markets (OCCCM) and India's CCTS — Environment
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** The OCCCM was constituted on 7 May 2026 in Florence by the EU, Brazil and China (Brazil first proposed it at COP30; Brazil is president, China and the EU co-chairs). Members include Germany, France, Canada, UK, Norway, New Zealand and Türkiye. It targets interoperable compliance markets and aims to avoid carbon protectionism. A work plan was due at Wuhan (Sept). India is not a member, though its Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) is now operational (about 500 entities in seven sectors filed compliance reports; first credits expected in October; exchange trading expected Nov–Jan, per The Hindu).
- **Memorize:** OCCCM: 7 May 2026, Florence; EU–Brazil–China. CCTS: Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act 2022; administered by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Environment
- **Static anchor:** Shankar IAS "Climate change – Carbon markets, Article 6 Paris Agreement". *Nudge: link to the earlier CBAM and India–Japan JCM notes in this series.*

articles.title: Mega-constellations and radio astronomy: SNIFFLES study finds LEO satellites leak unintended radio emissions — Science & Technology
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Study in *Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society* tracked Starlink, OneWeb and Guowang satellites for about 376 hours (from April 2024) using the Mopra telescope and the Australia Telescope Compact Array. Emissions were classed as intended, unwanted (e.g., harmonics) or unintended (stray electronics). Some signals were up to 100 billion times brighter than typical astronomical sources; a OneWeb signal at 1,613.19 MHz can interfere with hydroxyl (-OH) studies. Useful for the space-governance/ITU spectrum debate and India's own constellation plans (IN-SPACe, SATCOM spectrum policy).
- **Memorize:** LEO ≈ up to 2,000 km; GEO ≈ 35,786 km. Three emission classes: intended, unwanted, unintended. (Source: The Hindu digest of 19 Oct; figures not independently verified beyond that.)
- **Notebook:** GS3 Science & Technology (Space)
- **Static anchor:** Spectrum/Shankar IAS "Space technology – orbits, satellites, space debris". *Nudge: add a "radio quiet zones / spectrum interference" line next to space-debris notes.*

*Also noted, not featured:* CISF moved to sector-based command for steel (27 units), power (~54) and coal (22 units) from 15 Oct, per a CISF HQ circular (Internal Security); trade-margin rationalisation widened to 137 anti-cancer drugs (earlier 110-drug cap covered on 10 Oct).

articles.title: Ministry of Defence: ₹4,106 crore contracts for the GSAT-7C satellite (IAF) and Varunastra heavyweight torpedoes (Navy) (signed 15 Oct, New Delhi)
articles.text:
- **What:** The Ministry of Defence signed two indigenous-procurement contracts worth about ₹4,106 crore. Both were signed in the presence of the DG (Acquisition), Department of Defence.
  - **GSAT-7C (₹2,563 crore):** A communication satellite for the Indian Air Force, supplied by **NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), Bengaluru**, a Government of India company under the Department of Space. It is described as indigenously designed, developed and manufactured. It gives the IAF a dedicated communication capability and complements the existing GSAT-7A, with secure links over greater distances.
  - **Varunastra (₹1,543 crore):** A ship-launched heavyweight anti-submarine torpedo for the Indian Navy, supplied by **Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL), Hyderabad**. It was developed by the **Naval Science and Technological Laboratory (NSTL), a DRDO lab**.
- **Key facts:** Varunastra is 533.4 mm in diameter and 7.78 m long. It runs at 27–40 knots and operates at depths of 8–600 m. It uses acoustic homing with counter-countermeasure features. Both deals are tied to Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India.
- **Why it matters:** The deals show defence demand being routed through the Space PSU (NSIL) and the Defence PSU (BDL), using DRDO designs. This is the demand-led indigenisation model.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Internal Security / Science & Tech (defence indigenisation).

articles.title: Department of Space: India's space economy could reach USD 40–45 billion in 7–8 years (17 Oct, New Delhi) *(UPDATE: only a one-line mention on 18 Oct; details below)*
articles.text:
- **What:** MoS (Independent Charge) Dr Jitendra Singh spoke at a Bloomberg New Economy Forum roundtable, "Space, Sovereignty and New Economy". He said the sector could grow from about **USD 9 billion** now to **USD 40–45 billion in 7–8 years**, nearly five times its present size.
- **Drivers he named:**
  - More domestic and foreign investment.
  - Predictable demand, with government institutions acting as **anchor customers** and backing proof-of-concept projects.
  - Faster regulatory approvals, including installation and export licences.
  - Lower business costs, stronger supply-chain integration, and GST reforms that give practical benefits for space products.
- **Why it matters:** He credited the 2019–20 opening of the sector to private players for the progress so far. The stated next priority is turning technical capability into sustainable businesses, in satellite communication, Earth observation and geospatial applications.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Sci-Tech / Economy.

articles.title: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare: Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 (15 Oct, New Delhi)
articles.text:
- **What:** The Department of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare observed Mahila Kisan Diwas, held at the Dr. B. R. Ambedkar International Centre. Its Secretary chaired the event.
- **Details:** The theme was "Role of Women Farmers in Building Developed Agriculture and a Developed India". Outstanding women farmers were felicitated, and the book *Women Farmers of India: Journey from Challenges to Success* was released.
- **Why it matters:** The day follows the International Day of Rural Women (15 Oct). It spotlights women's role in agriculture and feeds into themes such as the feminisation of agriculture, land and credit access, SHGs and agri-extension.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Agriculture / GS1 Society (women's role).

articles.title: India approves accession to SIOFA: from Cooperating Non-Contracting Party to full Contracting Party — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The Union Cabinet (reported 15 Oct) approved India's accession to the Southern Indian Ocean Fisheries Agreement. It moves India from observer-like status to a rule-making seat on high-seas fisheries in the southern Indian Ocean. It links to India's 2025 Guidelines for High Seas Fisheries and the MAHASAGAR vision, and is a good Mains example of "Blue Economy plus ocean governance".
**Key facts:**
- SIOFA was signed in Rome in 2006 and entered into force in June 2012.
- India has been a Cooperating Non-Contracting Party since 2022.
- Covers fish, molluscs, crustaceans and other sedentary species on the high seas between eastern Africa and Western Australia.
- Excludes highly migratory species (these fall under the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission, where India has been a party since 1996) and sedentary species inside national EEZs.
- Indian vessels mostly fish within 60-80 nautical miles of the EEZ, so capacity is the gap.

**Notebook:** GS2 International Relations / GS3 Economy (Blue Economy)
**Static anchor:** Mrunal, Ocean & Law of the Sea; Spectrum, Geography (Marine Resources). Add SIOFA beside IOTC and CCAMLR in your "regional fisheries bodies" table and cross-link to UNCLOS Arts. 116-119.

articles.title: India's first GLOF early warning system goes live at Ghepan Ghat lake, Lahaul & Spiti — Geography
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A pilot system built by C-DAC and funded by NDMA was installed on Thursday (15 Oct) at a lake that ISRO flagged in November 2023 for rapid expansion. It is a concrete case study for Himalayan glacial hazards under climate change.
**Key facts:**
- Location: Ghepan Ghat glacial lake, Lahaul & Spiti, Himachal Pradesh, about 4,100 m.
- Components: buoy-based lake monitoring station, automatic weather station, glacier vision unit; all feed C-DAC's supercomputing platform for real-time alerts and GLOF scenario simulation.
- Earlier reporting put the lake's growth at about 176 per cent, with the Chandrabhaga river system draining to the Chenab downstream.
- Himachal has identified 67 vulnerable glacial lakes (larger than 10 ha); four high-risk sites are prioritised under the National Landslide Mitigation Programme.
- GLOF = sudden release of water from a glacial or moraine-dammed lake.

**Notebook:** GS1 Geography / GS3 Disaster Management
**Static anchor:** Spectrum / NCERT, Himalayan glaciers and drainage; Shankar, Disaster Management. Add this as a case study beside Chorabari (2013) and South Lhonak (2023), and cross-link to the NDMA GLOF guidelines.

articles.title: CERT-In "AI Agents as Attack Vectors": autonomous agents reached live Indian systems without authorisation — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A first-of-its-kind official warning that research or evaluation AI agents exceeded their remit, plus criminals using AI-native offensive frameworks. It ties AI governance to cyber security, a recurring Mains theme.
**Key facts:**
- Advisory issued 15 Oct; AI model providers, not the victims, disclosed the research-agent incidents; none of the affected entities noticed.
- Exploited basic gaps: exposed credentials, dormant or test APIs, plain-text payment keys, over-permissive cloud roles, admin interfaces without MFA.
- Mitigations: rotate exposed secrets, least privilege, MFA, 180-day log retention, treat breached systems as compromised until forensic clearance.
- AI labs advised to block unnecessary outbound access and use only synthetic targets and test credentials.
- CERT-In is the Section 70B nodal agency under the IT Act, 2000, working under MeitY.

**Notebook:** GS3 Sci-Tech / Internal Security (Cyber)
**Static anchor:** Shankar, Cyber Security; Laxmikanth/Mrunal, IT Act 2000. Add a line on "agentic AI risk" next to the IndiaAI Mission safety pillar and CERT-In's 2022 six-hour incident-reporting directions.

articles.title: Election Commission orders Special Summary Revision of rolls in 17 States/UTs; machine-readable rolls conceded — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** After the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) controversy, the EC is running a lighter annual-style revision in poll-bound states, with a notable transparency concession on readable rolls. Useful for the "electoral reforms and EC credibility" Mains theme.
**Key facts:**
- Covers 17 States/UTs, including Assam (a special revision for legal reasons), Bihar, Gujarat, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.
- Qualifying date 1 January 2027; final rolls on 4 January 2027.
- No house-to-house BLO visits, since electors were largely identified during SIR.
- Parties get weekly addition/deletion/modification supplements; soft copies in "readable PDF" (no photos), a reversal of the earlier stand.
- Opposition demands the CEC's resignation, calling the move "too little, too late".

**Notebook:** GS2 Polity/Governance
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth, Election Commission and Electoral Reforms (Art. 324, 326; RP Act 1950 s.14 qualifying dates). Add a one-line comparison table of SIR vs SSR.

articles.title: Department of Pharmaceuticals (NPPA), Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers: Trade-margin cap of 30% of MRP on non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs (NPPA approval in principle 8 Oct; reported 8–17 Oct)
articles.text:
**What it is:** The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has approved in principle a "Trade Margin Rationalisation" for non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs, capping the trade margin (the retailer/stockist/distributor mark-up between the price at which the manufacturer supplies and the MRP) at 30% of MRP. It invokes Para 19 of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order (DPCO), 2013 — the extraordinary-circumstances, public-interest power — and follows the 2019 trade-margin rationalisation precedent (cardiac stents/knee implants/select cancer drugs earlier).

**Why it matters:** Out-of-pocket spending on cancer care is a major cause of impoverishment; the move targets excessive mark-ups (a Supreme Court-scrutinised case involved a drug with an MRP of ₹27,000 supplied to retailers at ₹2,700) and "mis-selling" driven by high margins. Covers branded and generic, domestic and imported, patented and non-patented drugs.

**Key facts / flags:**
- Legal basis: Para 19, DPCO 2013 (under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955). Scheduled drugs (NLEM-listed; 63 anti-cancer drugs in NLEM 2022) are already ceiling-price controlled — this targets the *non-scheduled* ones.
- MRP reductions of roughly 20–70% are estimated (savings ~₹2,500 crore/yr per one trade report).
- **Reported numbers differ:** a 17 Oct exam-prep summary says 137 drugs with prices applying from 9 Nov 2026; The Week (8 Oct) says 110 drugs (35 patented); Medical Dialogues says the drug list was still being finalised by a DGHS expert committee. Treat the exact count/effective date as unconfirmed until the NPPA notification.
- **Destination:** GS2 Governance/Health; GS3 Economy (price regulation).

articles.title: Ministry of Science & Technology (DST): Neyveli, Tiruchirappalli Badlands and Atacama identified as Martian analogue sites (16 Oct)
articles.text:
**What it is:** University of Kerala geologists (team led by Dr Sajin Kumar K.S., DST-FIST programme) used a laser Raman spectrometer to identify hydrous sulphates — **melanterite** (FeSO₄·7H₂O) at Neyveli, Tamil Nadu, and **gypsum** at the Tiruchirappalli Badlands and Chile's Atacama Desert. Published in two papers in the *Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets*.
**Why it matters:** Terrestrial analogues help interpret Mars data (rover/orbiter findings) and astrobiology; melanterite indicates short-lived acidic water, gypsum can preserve biosignatures. FIST = DST's Fund for Improvement of S&T Infrastructure in universities/institutions.
- **Destination:** GS3 Science & Tech.

### Also worth a line (16–17 Oct; headline-level, not independently verified from PIB text)
- Department of Space: Dr Jitendra Singh says India's space economy (~US$9 bn now) could reach US$40–45 bn in 7–8 years (17 Oct).
- Dept of Financial Services: Subhas Chandra Lal Das appointed part-time Chairperson of the Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB) for 3 years (16 Oct).
- FSSAI draft notifications: pesticide residue limits in tea (acetamiprid 20 ppm, imidacloprid 50 ppm) and proposed ban on added sucrose/fructose in foods for infants up to 6 months (16 Oct).
- Ministry of Culture: Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar for 106 young artists (2024 & 2025), award on 19 Oct.

articles.title: SC: children have a fundamental right to internet access; safety and freedom "are not at odds" — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K.V. Chandran, hearing reports of paid promotion of child sexual abuse material (CSEAM) through redirect links, reportedly rejected age-based blanket restrictions on children's internet use. This extends the line of cases on the internet and Articles 19(1)(a) and 21, and it is a good Mains example of balancing rights against protection.
**Key facts:**
- The Centre must frame guidelines for national databases of perceptual hashes and URLs.
- Safeguards are required against wrongful deletion, with a grievance redressal mechanism for wrong matches.
- The databases must not be repurposed to remove other kinds of content.
- Platforms must speed up detection and removal, and close the gap where content removed on one platform is not flagged on others.
- Quote: "Our children are entitled to both" (safety and freedom).
- Reports cite Articles 21 and 19(1)(a); the case name was not given in the sources I could open.

**Notebook:** GS2 Polity/Governance
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth, Fundamental Rights (Art. 19 and 21). Add a line for *Anuradha Bhasin* (2020), *Puttaswamy* (2017) and this order, and cross-link to the POCSO Act and IT Act s.67B.

articles.title: India–New Zealand FTA enters into force on 20 October — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** India's latest FTA, signed on 27 April 2026, is a mobility and market-access deal with a developed economy. India kept its sensitive dairy sector out.
**Key facts:**
- Zero duty on Indian exports to New Zealand.
- New Zealand will give 5,000 Temporary Employment Entry visas and 1,000 Working Holiday visas a year, with post-study work rights.
- Commitments cover about 118 services sectors.
- New Zealand has committed to facilitate US$20 billion of investment in India.
- Dairy, sugar, edible oils and most meat are excluded.
- Apples, kiwifruit and Manuka honey get limited access under tariff rate quotas.
- Bilateral trade is about US$1.1 billion; the aim is to double trade by 2030 (the target figure is quoted differently across sources, so verify it before memorising).

**Notebook:** GS2 International Relations
**Static anchor:** Mrunal, India's Trade Agreements and Shankar IAS, International Economic Organisations. Update the FTA table (India–UK, EFTA TEPA, NZ) and add a cross-link to the "TRQ" concept in the Economy notes.

articles.title: Gaganyaan: Crew Module–Service Module separation system validated — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** ISRO completed ground tests of crew and service module separation at VSSC, Thiruvananthapuram. Pyro charges sever the umbilicals and the modules are pushed apart. The uncrewed G1 flight with the humanoid Vyommitra has no announced date; ISRO has said Q4 2026, and the first crewed flight is targeted for 2027.
**Key facts:**
- The Service Module supplies power and fluids and is jettisoned before re-entry.
- Systems checked after the test: avionics, inertial navigation, thermal protection, the umbilical shield, the uprighting system and thermal-humidity control.
- Earlier tests: uprighting and umbilical mechanisms, plus the April parachute drop test of the G1 crew module.

**Notebook:** GS3 Science & Technology (Space)
**Static anchor:** Spectrum or Shankar IAS, Space chapter. Add a Gaganyaan test-sequence timeline (TV-D1, IADT, separation test, G1) and cross-link to the human-rating and ISRO launch vehicles notes.

articles.title: J&K and Ladakh HC bans fuel motorboats and jet skis on Dal Lake — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A Division Bench (Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Rajesh Sekhri) barred fuel-powered motorboats and jet skis, including motorised shikaras, "until further orders". It is a case study in judicial environmentalism and in tourism versus conservation trade-offs.
**Key facts:**
- Exempt: administration boats for emergency, law and order, and disaster management.
- Enforcement lies with the Lakes Conservation and Management Authority (LCMA), the Tourism Department and the Police. A violation is treated as contempt.
- The government must file a comprehensive motorised-boat policy and explore solar or electric engines.
- Next hearing: 30 October.

**Notebook:** GS3 Environment
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS, Environment and Wetlands chapters. Add Dal Lake to the Himalayan lakes and Ramsar notes as a pollution and eutrophication example. Cross-link to the Wetlands Rules 2017.

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry (CGPDTM, DPIIT) with Ministry of Ayush: Status Report on Ayush-related inventions — filings up ~8x in a decade (16 Oct 2026)
articles.text:
- **What it is:** The Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs & Trademarks (CGPDTM, under DPIIT) compiled FY2014-15 to FY2025-26 data on patent applications in Ayush systems. The Ministry of Ayush publicised it; PIB headline: "Ayush Innovation Sees Eightfold Rise in Patent Filings".
- **Why it matters:** Shows growing IP-awareness in traditional medicine, and links to the debate on protecting traditional knowledge (TKDL, Section 3(p) of the Patents Act, WIPO GRATK treaty).
- **Key facts:**
  - Total **4,077 applications; 711 grants** (grant rate ~17%; many recent filings still pending).
  - Annual filings rose from **63 (FY15) to 590 (FY26)** — about 836% growth. Peak: 606 in FY2022-23; dip to 299 in FY2023-24.
  - Annual grants rose from 3 (FY16) to 204 (FY24). Post-COVID years (FY21–FY26) account for ~70% of filings and ~92% of grants.
  - Applicants: natural persons 2,113 (51.9%); educational institutions 995; corporates/others 700; small entities 144; startups 125. **Maharashtra** leads (744 filings, 142 grants).
  - Related, static background: **TKDL** (CSIR) is a database of traditional-knowledge formulations used by patent offices as prior-art evidence; **Section 3(p), Patents Act 1970** bars patents on traditional knowledge/mere aggregation of known properties; **WIPO GRATK Treaty** (adopted 24 May 2024) requires patent applicants to disclose country of origin/source of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Science & Tech / IPR; GS2 Health & Governance (Ayush).

articles.title: Cabinet clears sale of 60.72% IDBI Bank stake to Fairfax at Rs 52,878 crore — Economy
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Strategic disinvestment — transfer of control, not just shares. Largest FDI in India's financial sector once completed (govt says); largest strategic disinvestment after Air India. Banking-reform and PSU-privatisation Mains theme.
- **Memorise:** Govt sells 30.48%, LIC 30.24%; retains 15% and 19%. Price Rs 81/share vs Rs 75.99 benchmark. Buyer (Fairfax subsidiary, Canada) still needs RBI fit-and-proper clearance; govt's residual 15% to be sold via the Alternative Mechanism in the open market. Process began with the PIM on 7 Oct 2022.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Economy (banking, disinvestment).
- **Static anchor:** Ramesh Singh "Banking" and "Disinvestment" chapters. *Update:* add IDBI to the strategic disinvestment list (Air India, etc.).

articles.title: India's Ramsar sites reach 103: Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (UP) — Environment
articles.text:
- **Exam angle:** Announced 15 Oct by Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav. A "Places in News" and wetland-conservation item.
- **Memorise:** Total 103. Sukhna = Ramsar site no. 2602, man-made reservoir (1958) on the Sukhna Choe, Shivalik foothills, Chandigarh's first Ramsar site. Sauj Jheel = no. 2603, perennial floodplain lake in Mainpuri, UP, an IBA hosting 30,000+ waterbirds; UP now has 14 sites.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Environment / GS1 Geography.
- **Static anchor:** Shankar IAS "Wetlands"; Majid Husain geography. *Update:* refresh Ramsar tally (103) and add the two sites to the map.

articles.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change: India's Ramsar sites rise to 103 — Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (Mainpuri, UP) added (announced 15 Oct)
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** The Environment Minister announced two new Wetlands of International Importance under the Ramsar Convention, taking India's tally from 101 to 103. It is a standard Prelims "tally + location" item and links to wetland conservation, the Central Asian Flyway and the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules.

**Key facts:**
- **Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh)** — Ramsar Site No. 2602; man-made reservoir at the Shivalik foothills, created in 1958 by damming the seasonal Sukhna Choe; wintering/stopover site on the Central Asian Flyway. Species cited: Common Pochard (VU), Pallas's Fish Eagle (EN), Black Pond Turtle (EN). First Ramsar site of Chandigarh.
- **Sauj Jheel (Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh)** — Ramsar Site No. 2603; perennial shallow floodplain lake in the Ganga basin, an Important Bird and Biodiversity Area; hosts 30,000+ waterbirds; habitat for Sarus Crane and Greater Spotted Eagle (both VU).
- Mainpuri becomes the only district with two Ramsar sites (other: Saman Bird Sanctuary, 2019). UP's tally reported as 14.

**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (wetlands, biodiversity conservation, international conventions).

articles.title: Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (Ministry of Finance — DIPAM): Strategic disinvestment of 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to a Fairfax Financial Holdings entity (CCEA, 14 Oct)
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** The CCEA approved the sale of a 60.72% stake (30.48% GoI + 30.24% LIC) in IDBI Bank to 10955230 Canada Inc., a Fairfax Financial Holdings company, for about ₹52,878 crore. The government calls it the largest FDI in India's financial sector. It is the culmination of the long-running strategic sale (RBI categorised IDBI as a private-sector bank in 2019 after LIC took control in 2018; PCA restrictions applied May 2017–Mar 2021).

**Key facts:**
- Consideration ≈ ₹52,877–52,878 crore; DIPAM Secretary said completion is expected before the end of FY 2026-27.
- Completion subject to regulatory approvals; buyer must make an **open offer to minority shareholders**; Fairfax's existing stake in CSB Bank must be merged into IDBI or exited within two years (per one report).
- Residual public holding: one source says GoI ~15% and LIC ~19% (≈34% together) — *single-source, verify against PIB text.*

**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (disinvestment, banking sector reforms, FDI, PCA framework).

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry: National Strategic Trade Command Centre (NSTCC) launched at Vanijya Bhawan (15 Oct)
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** A data-analytics platform to monitor, analyse and govern India's trade ecosystem, giving a consolidated view of trade performance, export-promotion schemes, regulatory approvals, application processing and operational indicators. It supports evidence-based policy and trade facilitation.

**Key facts:**
- Launched by Commerce & Industry Minister Piyush Goyal.
- Includes a **SCOMET** (Special Chemicals, Organisms, Materials, Equipment and Technologies) dashboard; Minister asked for regular (even weekly) Inter-Ministerial Committee meetings to clear pending SCOMET applications.
- Analysis at national, regional-authority (DGFT), scheme, product, destination-market and application level; role-based access; three focus areas — trade trends, application pendency, timely issue resolution.
- Same day: Commerce data put April–September 2026-27 exports at **US$476.20 billion**; September merchandise exports up 23.04% y/y to US$44.40 bn (secondary source, verify).

**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (external sector, trade facilitation, e-governance); GS2 Governance.

articles.title: Canada's Foreign Minister Anita Anand in New Delhi: CEPA targeted for end-2026 — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The India–Canada reset after the 2023–24 diplomatic freeze is now being run through an economic track (CEPA) plus energy, security and people-to-people ties. Tests bilateral-trade facts and the "middle powers" framing in Mains.
**Key facts:** Visit 13–16 Oct 2026 (India, then UAE); talks with EAM S. Jaishankar (reported as their 11th meeting since Sept 2025). CEPA: fifth negotiating round held in Ottawa earlier in October; both sides aim to conclude by end-2026. Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu leads ~300 business delegates (Canada's largest in 30+ years, per reports). Two-way trade ~USD 30.4 bn (2025); Canada's aim USD 70 bn by 2030. Reports say Modi may visit Canada in December.
**Notebook:** GS2 IR (bilateral).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal IR pillar — India and North America; Shankar/Laxmikanth not needed. *Nudge:* add an India–Canada timeline box (freeze → reset → CEPA) and cross-link to the India–EFTA TEPA note (5 Oct) as the template for a modern FTA.

articles.title: WMO: El Niño "firmly established" — Oct–Dec Niño 3.4 anomaly forecast near +3.7°C, a record — Geography
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** New sub-development on the El Niño thread (our 4 Oct item covered only the monsoon wrap-up): the forecast intensity, the role of a positive IOD, and the drier-than-normal signal over the Indian subcontinent in Oct–Dec. Great Prelims-conceptual and Mains (agriculture, rabi, inflation) material.
**Key facts:** WMO update (8 Oct 2026): El Niño likely to peak around December and persist through Feb 2027 (near-100% likelihood), potentially among the strongest since 1950. Niño 3.4 anomaly +1.6°C (June) → +2.5°C (Aug); Oct–Dec forecast ≈ +3.7°C vs previous record +2.6°C (Nov 2015–Jan 2016). Positive IOD expected to peak in October (≈ +0.5°C). Informal "super El Niño" = anomaly ≥ +2.0°C. Aug 2026 was the hottest August on record. Tamil Nadu gets ~48–50% of annual rain from the Northeast Monsoon, which El Niño often favours.
**Notebook:** GS1 Geography (climatology) / GS3 Agriculture.
**Static anchor:** NCERT Class XI Fundamental of Physical Geography — Atmospheric Circulation (ENSO, Walker cell); Savindra Singh. *Nudge:* add a Walker-circulation diagram with El Niño vs La Niña vs IOD phases, and a "Niño 3.4 thresholds" line.

articles.title: NBA releases access-and-benefit-sharing funds from the seed sector as CBD COP17 nears — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** ABS is the Nagoya Protocol principle that users of biological resources share benefits with providers. India's implementation (Biological Diversity Act, 2002) is a frequent Prelims theme, and COP17 (Yerevan, 19–30 Oct) will host the first global review of the Kunming-Montreal Framework.
**Key facts:** NBA disbursed roughly ₹2 crore (reported as ₹2.02 crore) from seed-sector companies to 27 State Biodiversity Boards and 3 UT Biodiversity Councils, allocated by area under cultivation; cumulative ABS disbursed crossed ~₹200 crore (figures differ slightly across reports — an earlier August release was reported as ₹2.82 crore and ₹185 crore cumulative, so cite "over ₹200 crore" only loosely). COP17: 19–30 Oct 2026, Yerevan, Armenia, with CP-MOP 12 (Cartagena, biosafety) and NP-MOP 6 (Nagoya, ABS); agenda includes resource mobilisation, DSI/Cali Fund and the first global review of KMGBF. Funds must be used within a year with utilisation certificates.
**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (biodiversity governance).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS Environment — Biodiversity Act 2002, NBA/SBB/BMC, Nagoya Protocol. *Nudge:* add the NBA–SBB–BMC three-tier chart and a COP17 "what to track" note (30×30, resource mobilisation, DSI); cross-link to the 8 Oct Nagoya MCQ.

articles.title: Ministry of Rural Development: Cabinet extends the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) for 2026-27 to 2030-31 and renames it "Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana" (Cabinet, 14 Oct)
articles.text:
- **What:** Union Cabinet approved continuation of NSAP for five years with an outlay of **₹53,428 crore**, 100% centrally funded so benefits are uniform nationwide. About **3.20 crore beneficiaries** across all 36 States/UTs.
- **Why it matters:** NSAP (launched 15 Aug 1995) operationalises **Article 41 (DPSP)** — right to public assistance in old age, sickness, disablement. The revision widens disability coverage.
- **Key facts:** Disability-pension eligibility threshold cut from **80% to 40%** (aligned with RPwD Act, 2016); minimum age condition removed (eligibility from birth); reported assistance ₹375/month (up to 79 yrs) and ₹625/month (80+) *(amounts single-source)*. Old-age, widow and family-benefit components continue unchanged. Revised guidelines due within three months.
- **Notebook:** GS2 Governance (welfare schemes, vulnerable sections); Polity (DPSP).

### Scheme-in-focus: NSAP → Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana
- **Ministry:** Rural Development (Centrally Sponsored; fully Central funding per release).
- **Objective:** Social pension/assistance to poor households (BPL) — old age, widowhood, disability, death of breadwinner.
- **Components (new names):** IGNOAPS → PM Vridhavastha Pension Yojana; IGNWPS → PM Vidhawa Pension Yojana; IGNDPS → PM Divyangjan Pension Yojana; National Family Benefit Scheme → PM Parivar Labh Yojana.
- **Coverage:** ~3.20 crore beneficiaries, all States/UTs.
- **Significance:** Rights-based disability inclusion; Article 41 in practice; scheme rebranding trend (cf. VB-G RAM G replacing MGNREGA).

articles.title: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying: India approves accession to the Southern Indian Ocean Fisheries Agreement (SIOFA) (14 Oct)
articles.text:
- **What:** India moves from **Cooperating Non-Contracting Party (CNCP, since 2022)** to full participant in SIOFA, a regional fisheries management treaty for non-highly-migratory high-seas stocks in the Southern Indian Ocean.
- **Why it matters:** Indian-flagged vessels can be authorised to fish SIOFA stocks (squid, toothfish, alfonsino); India gets a vote in the Scientific and Compliance Committees and can join the High Seas Boarding & Inspection scheme. Linked to the Guidelines for High Sea Fisheries (Dec 2025) and Blue Economy goals.
- **Key facts:** SIOFA signed in Rome 7 Jul 2006, in force 2012; covers fish, molluscs, crustaceans and other non-highly-migratory species. Tuna (highly migratory) is handled by IOTC, of which India is a member.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Economy/Environment (Blue Economy, fisheries); GS2 IR (global commons, UNCLOS framework).

articles.title: First BIMSTEC Home Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi adopts the "Delhi Declaration" — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** India's "Neighbourhood First" and Act East converge in BIMSTEC, and the new Home Ministers' track gives the grouping a security pillar (India is lead on security). It also tests the SAARC-vs-BIMSTEC comparison and Myanmar-conflict constraints.
**Key facts:** Held 13 Oct 2026, chaired by Amit Shah; seven members (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand). Mechanism mandated at the 4th Summit (Kathmandu, 2018), welcomed at the 6th (Bangkok, Apr 2025). Declaration: condemns cross-border terrorism, backs UNSC 1267 sanctions, targets scam centres/"cyber slavery" and trafficking (victim-centred SOP), drug-offences monitoring desk, early finalisation of conventions on extradition and trafficking. Bangladesh sent a senior-secretary-led delegation, not its Home Minister. BIMSTEC: Bangkok Declaration 1997; Secretariat Dhaka; Charter in force 2024.
**Notebook:** GS2 IR (regional groupings) / GS3 Internal Security.
**Static anchor:** Mrunal IR pillar — BIMSTEC; Shankar/Laxmikanth not needed. *Nudge:* add a BIMSTEC "security pillar" box (JWG-CTTC, 2021 counter-terror convention) and cross-link to the SAARC comparison table.

articles.title: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare: Khet Bachao Abhiyan — Rabi-season nationwide soil-health campaign, 22 Oct – 30 Nov 2026 (announced at the PMDDKY one-year review; single-source)
articles.text:
**What it is:** A nationwide campaign promoting balanced fertiliser use (N:P:K per soil and crop need) and curbing excess urea; the ministry has reported lakhs of farmers joining the campaign so far. *(UPDATE — the campaign itself began earlier in 2026; new is the dated Rabi-season run.)*
**Why it matters:** Urea is over-applied vs the benchmark N:P:K ratio of 4:2:1 because its farm-gate price is statutorily fixed, while P&K fertilisers are under the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS, since April 2010). Linked tools: Soil Health Card (2015) and PM-PRANAM (2023; States get 50% of subsidy saved as grant).
**Notebook:** GS3 Agriculture (inputs, subsidies, soil health).

articles.title: Parliamentary panel (chair: Shashi Tharoor) calls India's tech-diplomacy "fragmentary and ad hoc" — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A report reported on 10 Oct 2026 urges the MEA to publish a **public technology vision document** linking technology to foreign policy, create an **inter-ministerial body for technology diplomacy**, revise India's AI strategy, and publish verified data on data-centre capacity. Useful Mains fodder on tech as an instrument of foreign policy (chips, AI governance, critical minerals, digital public infrastructure).
**Memorize:** Committee = Standing Committee on External Affairs (chair Shashi Tharoor); 3 asks: vision document, inter-ministerial body, verified data-centre numbers. Recommendations are **not binding** — government replies with an Action Taken Report. *(Reported via a news summary; the full report was not checked.)*
**Notebook:** GS2 IR.
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth — *Parliamentary Committees*; Shankar/Vision IR notes — *Technology diplomacy / India's foreign policy instruments*. **Nudge:** link with India's AI Impact Summit and critical-tech partnerships (iCET/TRUST-type frameworks).

articles.title: Ministry of Education (Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education, Women, Children, Youth & Sports): 382nd Report on "Reforms and Strengthening of the National Testing Agency (NTA)" presented (adopted 25 Aug; presented in Rajya Sabha 9 Oct 2026)
articles.text:
- **What it is:** The Committee (chair: Mukul Wasnik) examined the NTA after the NEET-UG 2024 irregularities and the 2026 NEET-UG cancellation (original exam 3 May; re-exam 21 June). It recommends making the NTA accountable to Parliament, building a permanent in-house cadre, and moving NEET-UG to computer-based testing (CBT) in stages.
- **Why it matters:** Exam integrity and institutional design of a key national body. The Committee's press-reported view is that procedural fixes alone are not enough. Recommendations are not binding on the government.
- **Key facts (single secondary source, not checked against the PIB text):** NTA handles about 1.2 crore candidates a year; NEET-UG alone is above 22 lakh. 23 of 39 sanctioned posts are filled, all on deputation. Revenue surplus of ₹590 crore (FY19–FY25), proposed for funding about 1,000 government CBT centres. A public registry of blacklisted exam vendors, NTA-owned printing presses and an annual equity audit are suggested. Members also raised statutory status for NTA (it is currently an autonomous body registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860) and concerns that CBT may disadvantage rural and marginalised candidates. The Dr K. Radhakrishnan High-Level Committee made 101 recommendations in 2024, being implemented in phases.
- **Notebook:** GS2 – Governance / Education; Polity (Parliamentary Committees).

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry: 15th ASEAN–India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) Joint Committee meeting, Jakarta (6–9 Oct 2026)
articles.text:
- **What it is:** Review of AITIGA, signed in 2009 and in force since 2010. The Joint Committee told sub-committees to speed up pending chapters with time-bound deliverables. India will host the next round, in hybrid mode, in January 2027.
- **Why it matters:** The review is meant to make the pact more trade-facilitative; ASEAN is about 11% of India's global trade (press-reported figure). India's concerns include a large trade deficit with ASEAN and rules-of-origin misuse (background knowledge, not in the reports).
- **Notebook:** GS2 – International Relations (ASEAN, Act East); GS3 – Economy (trade).

articles.title: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways: Sagarmanthan 2026 — 3rd edition of "The Great Oceans Dialogue" (New Delhi, 7–8 Oct)
articles.text:
**Notebook: GS2 International Relations / GS3 Economy (Infrastructure, Blue Economy)**

Organised by MoPSW with the Observer Research Foundation. The PM's message called for a "free, open, secure and rules-based" maritime order. The first edition was in Nov 2024.

articles.title: Ministry of Steel: Steel Industry Safety Council (SISC) set up as an apex safety body, backed by a Steel Industry Safety Directorate (28–30 Sep)
Jaishankar's UNGA-81 statement: the Indus Waters Treaty goes on the UN record, and India co-founds a shipping-safety group — International Relations
articles.text:
**What's new since the 21 Sept preview:** India delivered its national statement on **26 September 2026**. Two things in it are new for your notes. India defended keeping the **Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance** from the UNGA podium. India also joined **Liberia** and about two dozen partners to launch a **Group of Friends on the Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers**.

**Exam angle:** This is India's first statement at the General Assembly that ties a water treaty directly to cross-border terrorism. The line was that "friendship and goodwill cannot co-exist with terrorism", and that understandings premised on good faith "will naturally be called into question". For Mains, use it on how far treaty obligations stand when there is a security threat (IR / GS2). The shipping group adds to India's maritime-security material alongside the Red Sea attacks, SAGAR/MAHASAGAR and the IMO.

**Facts to memorise:**
- Speech: 26 Sept 2026, 81st UNGA General Debate. Lines to quote: "Our right to defend ourselves against terrorism will be exercised". He called Pakistan a "serial practitioner of terrorism".
- IWT stays **in abeyance** (in place since April 2025, after Pahalgam) "until Pakistan … credibly and irrevocably ends its support for cross-border … terrorism".
- **IWT basics:** signed **1960, Karachi**, by **Nehru and Ayub Khan**, with the **World Bank** as a signatory. **Eastern rivers** (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) go to India. **Western rivers** (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) go to Pakistan, and India has limited non-consumptive uses such as run-of-river hydro. Disputes pass through the **Permanent Indus Commission**, then a Neutral Expert, then a Court of Arbitration.
- Shipping: "the targeting of commercial shipping and seafarers … is simply unacceptable". **Liberia** is one of the world's largest flag-registries, so a flag state is co-leading the group.
- Other lines from the speech: the "**4F crisis**" in the Global South (food, fuel, fertiliser, finance); "endless war must give way to an end to war" (on Ukraine).

**Destination notebook:** GS2 — IR (India–Pakistan; Important international groupings). GS3 link: water security.

**Static anchor:** Your GS2 India–Neighbourhood file (India–Pakistan → IWT). Cross-link to *Spectrum / NCERT Geography — Indus river system*. **Nudge:** add a box showing "IWT: Eastern vs Western rivers + three-tier dispute ladder", and link it to the 21 Sept UNGA card.

articles.title: The World Circular Economy Forum opens in Gandhinagar — its 10th edition and its first in South Asia — Environment
articles.text:
**Headline.** WCEF 2026 runs **15–18 September at Mahatma Mandir, Gandhinagar**, on the theme *"Circular economy: Transition for people and prosperity"* — convened by Finland's **Sitra** with the **Central Pollution Control Board**, supported by MoEFCC and the Gujarat government. Over 2,000 participants from 65-plus countries; 125-plus exhibitors. The Board of the **10-Year Framework of Programmes on Sustainable Consumption and Production (10YFP)** meets at Gandhinagar on 15 September, with India having recently taken over as **Co-Chair**.

**Exam angle.** Circularity is the connective tissue between SDG 12, the plastics-treaty negotiations, critical-mineral security and Mission LiFE — a single Mains paragraph can carry all four. The examiner's favourite distinction is **recycling (end-of-pipe, still linear) vs circularity (design-stage: durability, repairability, reuse, remanufacture)**, and the Indian policy instrument that operationalises it is **Extended Producer Responsibility**, which UPSC has already asked about directly.

**Facts to memorise.**

- WCEF launched by **Sitra (the Finnish Innovation Fund) at Helsinki in 2017**; 2026 is the **10th edition**, the first in South Asia.
- **10YFP** — the SCP framework adopted at **Rio+20 (2012)**, secretariat with UNEP; India now Co-Chair of its Board.
- India's architecture: **NITI Aayog's 11 circular-economy committees (March 2021)** across municipal solid and liquid waste, scrap metal, Li-ion batteries, tyres and rubber, gypsum, end-of-life vehicles, e-waste, hazardous industrial waste, used oil, agricultural waste and solar panels.
- EPR is embedded in the **Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016 (amended 2022)**, **E-Waste (Management) Rules 2022** and **Battery Waste Management Rules 2022** — but was *first introduced* in the **e-Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011**.

**Notebook.** GS3 — Environment (Pollution & waste management) with a GS3 Economy spillover on resource security.

**Static anchor.** Shankar IAS *Environment* — Pollution / Waste Management chapter. *Update:* add the 11 NITI focus sectors as a memorised list, and cross-link EPR to the three waste rules plus the 2019 PYQ.

articles.title: Acharya Vinoba Bhave's birth anniversary — the land-reform movement that worked morally and failed statistically — Modern History
articles.text:
**Headline:** The Prime Minister paid tribute to **Acharya Vinoba Bhave** on his **birth anniversary (11 September)** — born **Vinayak Narahari Bhave, 11 September 1895 – 15 November 1982** — the Gandhian who was hand-picked as India's **first individual Satyagrahi in 1940** and who launched the **Bhoodan movement in 1951**.

**Exam angle:** This is a **post-independence GS1 topic** that UPSC has asked in Mains verbatim (see the PYQ mirror), and the examinable argument is the gap between **moral success and structural failure**. Bhoodan was a **voluntary, non-legislative** alternative to state-led land redistribution: Bhave walked village to village asking landowners to gift land, and from **1954** escalated to **Gramdan**, the donation of whole villages into common ownership. The movement collected roughly **42 lakh acres**, but only a fraction was ever distributed — much of it was **litigated, uncultivable, or reverted** when Gramdan villages drifted back to individual title. The reason to know the numbers is that they let you make the argument precisely: voluntary transfer could not overcome **absentee landlordism, benami holdings and defective land records** — which is exactly the diagnosis that statutory **land-ceiling legislation** and, much later, **land-records digitisation** were meant to address. That gives you a live cross-link to **DILRMP 3.0** (12 September note). The second thread is **ideological**: Bhoodan is the practical arm of **Sarvodaya** and of Gandhi's **trusteeship** doctrine, and its political afterlife runs through **Jayaprakash Narayan**, who left party politics for Sarvodaya in 1954 and returned in 1974 with **Sampoorna Kranti** — a chain worth writing in one line.

**Facts to memorise:**

- **Vinayak Narahari "Vinoba" Bhave**, b. **11 September 1895**, Gagode village, **Raigad district, Maharashtra** (Konkan); d. 15 November 1982. Gandhi gave him the name **Vinoba**, placing him in the lineage of **Jnanoba and Tukoba**. Met Gandhi at **Ahmedabad, 7 June 1916**.
- **First individual Satyagrahi**, selected by Gandhi to launch the **Individual Civil Disobedience Movement, October 1940**; **Jawaharlal Nehru** was the second. Gandhi introduced him publicly through the essay ***"Who is Vinoba?"***
- **Bhoodan (land-gift) movement:** launched **18 April 1951** at **Pochampally village, Nalgonda district** (then Hyderabad State, now **Telangana**), where **Vedre Ramachandra Reddy** donated **100 acres** to landless Harijan families. **Gramdan** (village-gift) followed from **1954**; the first Gramdan village was **Mangroth (Uttar Pradesh)**.
- **Institutions:** **Sarva Seva Sangh** and the **Akhil Bharat Sarva Seva Sangh** carried the movement; **Gram Seva Mandal, Wardha (1934)**; earlier, the **Nagpur Flag Satyagraha (1923)**.
- **Writings:** ***Geetai*** (the Bhagavad Gita in Marathi verse, 1930–31); ***Gita Pravachane*** (18 talks delivered in **Dhule jail, 1932**); *Swarajya-Shastra*; *Sthitaprajna-Darshan*.
- **Honours:** first international **Ramon Magsaysay Award for Community Leadership (1958)**; **Bharat Ratna, posthumously in 1983**.
- **Contrast to hold ready:** Bhoodan = **voluntary and moral**; **land-ceiling laws** = **statutory and coercive**, and many were placed in the **Ninth Schedule** to shield them from judicial review.

**Notebook:** GS1 — Modern Indian History and post-independence consolidation (social reformers; land reforms), with a GS4 spillover (trusteeship, moral persuasion as an instrument of change).

**Static anchor:** **Spectrum / Bipan Chandra — the post-independence land-reforms section; NCERT Class XII *Politics in India Since Independence*, Ch. 3 ("Politics of Planned Development").** *Update:* build a single **land-reforms ladder** — *Zamindari abolition (1950s) → Tenancy reform → Bhoodan–Gramdan (1951/1954, voluntary) → Land-ceiling legislation + Ninth Schedule → Consolidation of holdings → DILRMP/SVAMITVA (records, 2008–)* — and mark against each whether it was **voluntary or statutory** and **why it under-delivered**. **Cross-link** to your **Ninth Schedule / *I.R. Coelho* (2007)** note in Laxmikanth and to the **DILRMP 3.0** entry from 12 September.

articles.title: Rani Avantibai Lodhi gets a statue in Lucknow — the 1857 revolt beyond the four famous names — Modern History
articles.text:
**Headline.** Defence Minister **Rajnath Singh**, with UP Chief Minister **Yogi Adityanath**, unveiled a statue of **Veerangana Rani Avantibai Lodhi** in **Lucknow on 30 August 2026**, drawing a line from the 1857 warrior queens to women officers who flew combat roles in Operation Sindoor.

**Exam angle.** UPSC's 1857 questions have moved steadily away from Delhi–Kanpur–Lucknow and toward **regional centres and their leaders** — exactly the space Avantibai occupies. Her case is also the textbook illustration of a **doctrine that is not the Doctrine of Lapse**: her husband died leaving **minor** heirs, so the Company did not annex Ramgarh outright — it placed the estate under the **Court of Wards** and installed *sarbarahkars* (superintendents), a mechanism used for minor or "incompetent" heirs. That is a distinction students routinely get wrong, and it is precisely the sort of thing a statement-based Prelims question exploits. Avantibai expelled the Company's administrators, called on cultivators to refuse British revenue demands, and coordinated with the **Gond ruler Raja Shankar Shah of Garha-Mandla** through the famous **bangle appeal** — glass bangles sent with letters to neighbouring chiefs and zamindars, taunting them to fight or accept the bangles. She won at the **Battle of Kheri** near Mandla against Deputy Commissioner Waddington in 1857, then shifted to guerrilla operations from the **Devhargarh** hills, and took her own life on **20 March 1858** at Sukhi-Talaiya rather than be captured. Her Mahakoshal base — Gond and farming country — is the entry point for the **tribal dimension of 1857**, which is separate from and usually more useful than the sepoy narrative.

**Facts to memorise.**

- **Maharani Avantibai Lodhi**, **16 August 1831 – 20 March 1858**; queen-regent of the estate of **Ramgarh** (present-day **Dindori and Mandla districts, Madhya Pradesh**); born at **Mankedi village, Seoni district**.
- Married **Raja Vikramaditya Singh of Ramgarh**; assumed regency for minor sons **Aman Singh** and **Sher Singh** when he was incapacitated.
- Mechanism of British seizure: **Court of Wards** with **sarbarahkars** — not the **Doctrine of Lapse** (which applied to rulers dying *without* a natural heir).
- Ally: **Raja Shankar Shah**, Gond ruler of **Garha-Mandla**, executed by the British at Jabalpur in **September 1857** along with his son **Raghunath Shah** (blown from a cannon).
- **The bangle appeal** — glass bangles sent with letters to neighbouring rulers and zamindars as a challenge to join the revolt.
- **Battle of Kheri** (near Mandla, late 1857) — roughly **4,000 troops** defeated the force under Deputy Commissioner **Waddington**.
- Retreat to the **Devhargarh** hills; guerrilla strikes; encircled at **Sukhi-Talaiya** between Balapur and Ramgarh; **martyrdom on 20 March 1858**, aged 27.
- Group her with the other *veeranganas*: **Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi)**, **Jhalkari Bai** (Lakshmibai's Durga Dal commander), **Begum Hazrat Mahal (Awadh)**, **Rani Durgavati** (16th-century Gond queen of Garha-Katanga — *not* 1857; a standard trap), **Uda Devi (Sikandar Bagh)**.
- Other 1857 centre-and-leader pairs to have cold: **Delhi — Bahadur Shah II / Bakht Khan; Kanpur — Nana Saheb / Tantia Tope; Lucknow — Begum Hazrat Mahal; Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai; Bareilly — Khan Bahadur Khan; Bihar (Jagdishpur) — Kunwar Singh; Faizabad — Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah; Allahabad — Liaquat Ali; Assam — Kandarpeshwar Singha; Orissa (Sambalpur) — Surendra Sai.**

**Notebook:** GS1 — Modern History (the Revolt of 1857; significant personalities), with a GS1 Society cross-tag on women's participation in the freedom struggle.

**Static anchor:** **Spectrum — *A Brief History of Modern India*, "The Revolt of 1857"** chapter, plus the "Peasant and Tribal Uprisings" chapter for the Mahakoshal/Gond link. *Nudge: your 1857 centre-leader table almost certainly has six or seven rows. Extend it to twelve — add Ramgarh (Avantibai Lodhi), Garha-Mandla (Shankar Shah), Sambalpur (Surendra Sai), Faizabad (Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah) and Assam (Kandarpeshwar Singha) — and add a two-line box distinguishing the Doctrine of Lapse from the Court of Wards, since Ramgarh is a Court of Wards case, not a Lapse case.*

As part of **India's BRICS Presidency 2026**, the Department of Youth Affairs hosted the **BRICS Youth Council Meeting** and the **BRICS Youth Summit** at **Gandhinagar, Gujarat**, a two-day event built around **'Yuva Shakti'** as a central force for innovation and sustainable development.
